narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated an 88.2% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. This is a high-risk estimate, not a certainty, but it was strong enough to lead to rejection.

The most important factor was your third-year class standing. You are in the lowest decile, while accepted students average around the middle of their class, and this pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Your first-year standing, also much lower than the accepted average, pushed in the same direction, though less strongly. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.50 was above the accepted average of 3.23, and it was the main factor working in your favor, pushing toward passing. It was simply not enough to outweigh the concerns about your law school performance.

To move forward, contact the admissions office to ask whether the decision can be reconsidered or deferred and what additional context they will accept. Ask for academic advising focused on bar readiness, consider structured bar preparation and support before retaking, and improve any remaining admissions credentials, such as retaking the LSAT if feasible.
